### 2020

::: {.question-card}
### 2020 May/June · 9231/21 & 9231/22 · Question 5 · 11 marks

The curves $C_1:y=\cosh x$ and $C_2:y=\sinh 2x$ intersect at the point where $x=a$.

**(a)** Find the exact value of $a$, giving your answer in logarithmic form. **[4]**

**(b)** Sketch $C_1$ and $C_2$ on the same diagram. **[2]**

**(c)** Find the exact value of the length of the arc of $C_1$ from $x=0$ to $x=a$. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

**(a)** At the intersection, $\cosh a=\sinh 2a=2\sinh a\cosh a$. Since $\cosh a\neq0$,

$$
\sinh a=\frac12.
$$

Using the logarithmic form of $\sinh^{-1}$,

$$
\boxed{a=\sinh^{-1}\!\left(\frac12\right)
=\ln\left(\frac12+\sqrt{\frac14+1}\right)
=\ln\left(\frac12+\frac{\sqrt5}2\right)}.
$$

**(b)** $C_1$ is the even U-shaped curve $\cosh x$, and $C_2$ is the odd increasing curve $\sinh 2x$. They intersect in the first quadrant at $x=a=\ln\left(\frac12+\frac{\sqrt5}2\right)$ and, by symmetry, also at $x=-a$.

**(c)** For $C_1:y=\cosh x$,

$$
\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\sinh x,
\qquad
\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\right)^2}
=\sqrt{1+\sinh^2x}
=\cosh x.
$$

Hence

$$
s=\int_0^a\cosh x\,\mathrm dx
=\bigl[\sinh x\bigr]_0^a
=\sinh a
=\boxed{\frac12}.
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-2020-mj-21-22-q5"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/21/M/J/2020, Q5; 9231/22/M/J/2020, Q5.</div>
:::

### 2020 May/June · 9231/23 · Question 6(a) · 3 marks

Starting from the definitions of $\tanh$ and $\operatorname{sech}$ in terms of exponentials, prove that

$$
1-\tanh^2\theta=\operatorname{sech}^2\theta.
$$

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Starting from

$$
\tanh\theta=\frac{e^\theta-e^{-\theta}}{e^\theta+e^{-\theta}},\qquad
\operatorname{sech}\theta=\frac2{e^\theta+e^{-\theta}},
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
1-\tanh^2\theta
&=1-\left(\frac{e^\theta-e^{-\theta}}{e^\theta+e^{-\theta}}\right)^2\\
&=\frac{(e^\theta+e^{-\theta})^2-(e^\theta-e^{-\theta})^2}{(e^\theta+e^{-\theta})^2}\\
&=\frac4{(e^\theta+e^{-\theta})^2}\\
&=\boxed{\operatorname{sech}^2\theta}.
\end{aligned}
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-2020-mj-23-q6a"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/23/M/J/2020, Q6(a).</div>
:::

### 2020 October/November · 9231/21 & 9231/23 · Question 8(a)–(b) · 5 marks

**(a)** Sketch the graph of $y=\coth x$ for $x\geqslant0$ and state the equations of the asymptotes. **[2]**

**(b)** Starting from the definitions of $\coth$ and $\operatorname{cosech}$ in terms of exponentials, prove that

$$
\coth^2x-\operatorname{cosech}^2x=1.
$$

**[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

**(a)** For $x\geqslant0$, $y=\coth x$ starts at the vertical asymptote $x=0$ and decreases towards $y=1$.

{{< include figures/hyperbolic/graph-coth.svg >}}

The asymptotes are

$$
\boxed{x=0\ \text{and}\ y=1}.
$$

**(b)** Starting from

$$
\coth x=\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}{e^x-e^{-x}},\qquad
\operatorname{cosech}x=\frac2{e^x-e^{-x}},
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\coth^2x-\operatorname{cosech}^2x
&=\left(\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}{e^x-e^{-x}}\right)^2-\left(\frac2{e^x-e^{-x}}\right)^2\\
&=\frac{e^{2x}+2+e^{-2x}-4}{(e^x-e^{-x})^2}\\
&=\frac{e^{2x}-2+e^{-2x}}{(e^x-e^{-x})^2}\\
&=1.
\end{aligned}
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-2020-on-21-23-q8ab"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/21/O/N/2020, Q8(a)–(b); 9231/23/O/N/2020, Q8(a)–(b).</div>
:::

### 2021

::: {.question-card}
### 2021 May/June · 9231/21 & 9231/22 · Question 7 · 10 marks

It is given that

$$
y=\operatorname{sech}^{-1}\left(x+\frac12\right).
$$

**(a)** Express $\cosh y$ in terms of $x$ and hence show that

$$
\sinh y\,\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=-\frac1{\left(x+\frac12\right)^2}.
$$

**[3]**

**(b)** Find the first three terms in the Maclaurin's series for $\operatorname{sech}^{-1}\left(x+\frac12\right)$ in the form

$$
\ln a+bx+cx^2,
$$

where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are constants to be determined. **[7]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

**(a)** Since $\operatorname{sech}y=x+\dfrac12$,

$$
\boxed{\cosh y=\left(x+\frac12\right)^{-1}}.
$$

Differentiating $\operatorname{sech}y=x+\dfrac12$ with respect to $x$,

$$
-\operatorname{sech}y\tanh y\,\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=1.
$$

Using $\operatorname{sech}y\tanh y=\dfrac{\sinh y}{\cosh^2y}=\sinh y\left(\operatorname{sech}y\right)^2$,

$$
\sinh y\,\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=-\left(\operatorname{sech}y\right)^2
=\boxed{-\frac1{\left(x+\frac12\right)^2}}.
$$

**(b)** At $x=0$,

$$
y(0)=\operatorname{sech}^{-1}\!\left(\frac12\right)
=\cosh^{-1}2=\ln\left(2+\sqrt3\right).
$$

From part (a),

$$
y'(0)=-\frac1{\left(\frac12\right)^2\sinh y(0)}
=-\frac4{\sinh(\cosh^{-1}2)}
=-\frac4{\sqrt3}.
$$

Differentiating

$$
\sinh y\,y'=-\left(x+\frac12\right)^{-2}
$$

gives, at $x=0$,

$$
\sinh y\,y''+\cosh y\,(y')^2=2\left(x+\frac12\right)^{-3}
\;\Longrightarrow\;
\sqrt3\,y''(0)+\frac{16}{3}=16,
$$

so $y''(0)=\dfrac{16}{3\sqrt3}$. Hence

$$
\boxed{y=\ln\left(2+\sqrt3\right)-\frac4{\sqrt3}x+\frac8{3\sqrt3}x^2}.
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-2021-mj-21-22"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/21/M/J/2021, Q7; 9231/22/M/J/2021, Q7.</div>
:::

### 2021 May/June · 9231/23 · Question 6(a) · 3 marks

Starting from the definitions of $\sinh$ and $\cosh$ in terms of exponentials, prove that

$$
2\sinh2x=\cosh2x-1.
$$

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Using

$$
\sinh2x=\frac{e^{2x}-e^{-2x}}2,\qquad
\cosh2x=\frac{e^{2x}+e^{-2x}}2,
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
2\sinh2x
&=2\left(\frac{e^{2x}-e^{-2x}}2\right)\\
&=e^{2x}-e^{-2x}\\
&=\frac{2e^{2x}-2e^{-2x}}2\\
&=\frac{e^{2x}+e^{-2x}}2-1\\
&=\boxed{\cosh2x-1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-2021-mj-23-q6a"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/23/M/J/2021, Q6(a).</div>
:::

### 2021 October/November · 9231/21 & 9231/23 · Question 8(a) · 3 marks

Starting from the definition of $\cosh$ in terms of exponentials, prove that

$$
2\cosh^2A=\cosh2A+1.
$$

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Starting from $\cosh A=\dfrac{e^A+e^{-A}}2$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
2\cosh^2A
&=2\left(\frac{e^A+e^{-A}}2\right)^2\\
&=\frac{e^{2A}+2+e^{-2A}}2\\
&=\frac{e^{2A}+e^{-2A}}2+1\\
&=\boxed{\cosh2A+1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-2021-on-21-23-q8a"> Completed</label>

:::

### 2022

::: {.question-card}
### 2022 May/June · 9231/21 & 9231/22 · Question 2 · 8 marks

**(a)** Starting from the definitions of $\cosh$ and $\sinh$ in terms of exponentials, prove that

$$
\cosh2x=2\sinh^2x+1.
$$

**[3]**

**(b)** Find the set of values of $k$ for which

$$
\cosh2x=k\sinh x
$$

has two distinct real roots. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

**(a)** Using $\cosh x=\dfrac{e^x+e^{-x}}2$ and $\sinh x=\dfrac{e^x-e^{-x}}2$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
2\sinh^2x+1
&=2\left(\frac{e^x-e^{-x}}2\right)^2+1\\
&=\frac{e^{2x}-2+e^{-2x}}2+1\\
&=\frac{e^{2x}+e^{-2x}}2\\
&=\boxed{\cosh2x}.
\end{aligned}
$$

**(b)** Using part (a),

$$
2\sinh^2x+1=k\sinh x
\;\Longrightarrow\;
2\sinh^2x-k\sinh x+1=0.
$$

This is a quadratic in $\sinh x$. It has two distinct real roots when its discriminant is positive:

$$
k^2-8>0.
$$

Therefore

$$
\boxed{k<-\sqrt8\ \text{or}\ k>\sqrt8}.
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-2022-mj-21-22-q2"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/21/M/J/2022, Q2; 9231/22/M/J/2022, Q2.</div>
:::

### 2023 May/June · 9231/21 · Question 8(a) · 3 marks

Starting from the definitions of $\operatorname{sech}$ and $\tanh$ in terms of exponentials, prove that

$$
1-\operatorname{sech}^2t=\tanh^2t.
$$

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Starting from

$$
\operatorname{sech}t=\frac2{e^t+e^{-t}},\qquad
\tanh t=\frac{e^t-e^{-t}}{e^t+e^{-t}},
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
1-\operatorname{sech}^2t
&=1-\left(\frac2{e^t+e^{-t}}\right)^2\\
&=\frac{(e^t+e^{-t})^2-4}{(e^t+e^{-t})^2}\\
&=\frac{e^{2t}+2+e^{-2t}-4}{(e^t+e^{-t})^2}\\
&=\frac{e^{2t}-2+e^{-2t}}{(e^t+e^{-t})^2}\\
&=\frac{(e^t-e^{-t})^2}{(e^t+e^{-t})^2}\\
&=\boxed{\tanh^2t}.
\end{aligned}
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-2023-mj-21-q8a"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/21/M/J/2023, Q8(a).</div>
:::

### 2023 October/November · 9231/21 & 9231/23 · Question 6(a) · 3 marks

Starting from the definitions of $\cosh$ and $\sinh$ in terms of exponentials, prove that

$$
\sinh2x=2\sinh x\cosh x.
$$

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Starting from

$$
\cosh x=\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}2,\qquad
\sinh x=\frac{e^x-e^{-x}}2,
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
2\sinh x\cosh x
&=2\left(\frac{e^x-e^{-x}}2\right)\left(\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}2\right)\\
&=\frac{(e^x-e^{-x})(e^x+e^{-x})}2\\
&=\frac{e^{2x}-e^{-2x}}2\\
&=\boxed{\sinh2x}.
\end{aligned}
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-2023-on-21-23-q6a"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/21/O/N/2023, Q6(a); 9231/23/O/N/2023, Q6(a).</div>
:::

### 2024 May/June · 9231/21 & 9231/22 · Question 6(a) · 2 marks

Show that

$$
\left(\cosh x+\sinh x\right)^{1/2}=e^{\frac12x}.
$$

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Substituting the exponential definitions,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\left(\cosh x+\sinh x\right)^{1/2}
&=\left(\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}2+\frac{e^x-e^{-x}}2\right)^{1/2}\\
&=\left(e^x\right)^{1/2}\\
&=\boxed{e^{\frac12x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

</details>

### 2025 May/June · 9231/23 · Question 2(a) · 3 marks

Starting from the definitions of $\tanh$ and $\operatorname{sech}$ in terms of exponentials, prove that

$$
\tanh^2t+\operatorname{sech}^2t=1.
$$

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Starting from

$$
\tanh t=\frac{e^t-e^{-t}}{e^t+e^{-t}},\qquad
\operatorname{sech}t=\frac2{e^t+e^{-t}},
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tanh^2t+\operatorname{sech}^2t
&=\left(\frac{e^t-e^{-t}}{e^t+e^{-t}}\right)^2+\left(\frac2{e^t+e^{-t}}\right)^2\\
&=\frac{e^{2t}-2+e^{-2t}+4}{(e^t+e^{-t})^2}\\
&=\frac{e^{2t}+2+e^{-2t}}{(e^t+e^{-t})^2}\\
&=1.
\end{aligned}
$$

</details>

### 2025 October/November · 9231/24 · Question 2 · 6 marks

**(a)** Find the exact values of $x$ for which

$$
\cosh 2x=6\sinh^2x,
$$

giving your answers in logarithmic form. **[4]**

**(b)** Sketch the curves $C_1:y=\cosh 2x$ and $C_2:y=6\sinh^2x$ on the same diagram. **[2]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

**(a)** Using $\cosh2x=1+2\sinh^2x$,

$$
1+2\sinh^2x=6\sinh^2x
\;\Longrightarrow\;
4\sinh^2x=1
\;\Longrightarrow\;
\sinh x=\pm\frac12.
$$

Therefore

$$
\boxed{x=\pm\ln\left(\frac12+\frac{\sqrt5}2\right)}.
$$

**(b)** $C_1:y=\cosh2x$ is even with minimum $(0,1)$; $C_2:y=6\sinh^2x$ is even, passes through the origin and increases rapidly. The curves intersect at

$$
x=\pm\ln\left(\frac12+\frac{\sqrt5}2\right),
$$

with $C_1$ above $C_2$ between these points and below it outside.

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-2025-on-24-q2"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/24/O/N/2025, Q2.</div>
:::
